images.seen: A small scruffy dog in a grey knitted jersey standing on dew-soaked grass at blue dawn, misty garden behind. Monday.
lines: The grass is wet, the air is cold, and the jersey was not optional.
Dew this heavy means the night got properly cold and stayed there.
Small dog, thick jersey, short patrol: winter mornings run on reduced hours.

images.seen: A mother kneeling at the front door zipping her son's puffer jacket over his school uniform and beanie, cold blue dawn and wet street outside. Wednesday.
lines: The zip goes all the way up today; the walk to the gate has teeth.
That jacket call was made by one look through the kitchen window.
Beanie plus puffer plus school tie: the cold front has reached the uniform.

images.seen: A Karoo farmer standing among his sheep at a whitewashed kraal wall at dawn, breath visible, pastel cold sky over the plain. Thursday.
lines: You can see his breath, and the sheep are wearing the only good answer.
The Karoo does its coldest hour right before its prettiest one.
The sheep bunched before he opened the gate; they read the cold first.

images.seen: An old sedan frosted white in a driveway at dawn, iced windscreen, bare trees and a pink band on the horizon. Tuesday.
lines: The sky is clear and the car is white, and those two facts are related.
That windscreen is a ten-minute job and the kettle knows its part.
The car coughed twice before it agreed to start.
